clue.text: Finish drinks with old fellows

parts.note: a round is a set of drinks bought for a group
F is the abbreviation for fellow, so two fellows give FF

explanation.surface: A pub evening winds up with a last round shared among some elderly companions.
explanation.definitionFit: To round off something is to complete it neatly, a phrasal synonym for finish.

clue.text: Stand up to relax one's parts

indicators.note: parts means splits apart, so the word for relax is opened to take the other letters

parts.note: to rest is to relax
one's is read as I'S, I being the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone stands up to a demand to relax parts of their body.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppose or withstand a pressure is to stand up to it.

clue.text: Major row from union in favour of a recount, initially

parts.note: pro means in favour of

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word recount

explanation.surface: A union calls for a recount, causing a big argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud public outcry or commotion is a major row.

clue.text: Officer allowed in river, uncovering parts of jugs

indicators.note: in says the officer and allowed letters sit within the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and another on the England-Wales border
Col is short for colonel
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: An officer is allowed into a river, oddly uncovering pottery jugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jugs' looks like crockery but is slang for breasts.
explanation.definitionFit: A low-cut neckline exposes the cleavage, so it uncovers parts of the bust.

clue.text: Clue for Yankee and his big day

definitions.meaning: Yankee is Y in the radio alphabet, and Y is the fourth letter of the month July
the American Independence Day is the great national holiday of a Yank

explanation.surface: A hint about an American and his special day.
explanation.definitionFit: US Independence Day is celebrated on that date, and Y is the fourth letter of the month.

clue.text: From space, circling, this can be seen receding

definitions.text: From space, circling, this can be seen receding

indicators.note: receding means moving back, so the hidden letters are read backwards
From says the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A satellite view shows a polar feature shrinking as the climate warms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' picks PACECI out of 'space, circling'; 'receding' turns it round. The whole clue also describes the answer, seen from orbit and shrinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Polar ice sheets are visible from orbit and are melting back as the planet warms.

clue.text: Screen 150 trees

parts.note: CL is 150 in Roman numerals
oak is a kind of tree, standing for trees in general

explanation.surface: A row of 150 trees forms a screen.
explanation.definitionFit: A cover that conceals something screens it, as in a cloak of secrecy.

clue.text: Plants grounds surrounding court

indicators.note: surrounding says the word for grounds goes round the court abbreviation

parts.note: grounds for something are its causes

explanation.surface: Plants are growing in the grounds around a tennis court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grounds' suggests land around a court, but it means reasons.
explanation.definitionFit: Desert succulents with spines are plants, here in a regular plural.

clue.text: Men Only organ writing about article in Times

indicators.note: about says the writing word goes around the other letters

parts.note: prose is ordinary writing

indicators.note: in says the article sits inside the two letters for times

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time, so times gives TT
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A piece in a men's magazine is written about an article in a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Men Only' looks like the old men's magazine title, but it means an organ only men have.
explanation.definitionFit: This gland is found only in the male body, an organ exclusive to men.

clue.text: Tree increasing? Get trimmer

parts.note: the spruce is a conifer
up means rising or increasing, as in prices being up

explanation.surface: A growing tree prompts the question whether it needs pruning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trimmer' suggests cutting a hedge, but here it means neater or smarter.
explanation.definitionFit: To smarten oneself and look neater is a phrasal verb meaning get trimmer.

clue.text: Woolly garment on child in river

indicators.note: in says the letters for on and child are placed within the river's name

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river

explanation.surface: A child wading in a river wears a woollen cape.
explanation.definitionFit: This South American cloak, a blanket with a head hole, is usually knitted or woven from wool.

clue.text: Cute EU author condemned catwalk display

indicators.note: condemned suggests something wrecked, so the letters of cute eu author are rearranged

explanation.surface: A writer from the European Union is denounced for a cute fashion show.
explanation.definitionFit: High fashion from leading designers is shown off by models on the runway.

clue.text: Stole first of summer fruit by lake

indicators.note: first of picks just the opening letter of the word summer

parts.note: a haw is the red berry of the hawthorn
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Someone pinched the first summer fruit from beside a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stole' reads as a past-tense verb, but it is the noun for a wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: A stole is a long scarf or wrap worn over the shoulders, a close synonym.

clue.text: Follow Hearts, maybe training in this?

parts.note: to track someone is to follow them
hearts is one example of a suit in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A football fan follows Hearts, the Edinburgh club, and wonders about the squad's training gear.
explanation.walkthrough: Heart of Midlothian (Hearts) is a Scottish football club, which fits the training picture, but here hearts is the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Athletes wear this zipped sportswear outfit while exercising, so it is what you train in.

clue.text: Not just teeth wobble about when drinking litres

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the litre letter goes inside the rearranged letters
about signals that the letters of teeth wobble are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone drinks so much that their teeth start wobbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges TEETH WOBBLE, and 'when drinking' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A blow or remark that is unfair breaks the rules of boxing, so it is not just.

clue.text: In general, possibly it might absorb kids in lockdown

definitions.text: it might absorb kids in lockdown

indicators.note: possibly hints the letters of in general can be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Generally, something may keep children occupied when schools are closed.
explanation.definitionFit: During pandemic school closures, children studied online at home, a form of remote study.

clue.text: Wacky hits, typical contents of men's drawers?

parts.note: odd means strange or wacky
to sock someone is to hit them

explanation.surface: Crazy punches are compared to what men keep in their chest of drawers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawers' might mean underpants, but here it is furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Men famously have unmatched hosiery rummaged loose in their bedroom chests of drawers.

clue.text: They give up introducing new underwear

indicators.note: introducing means bringing something in, so the letter for new goes inside

parts.note: people who kick a habit give it up, so they are kickers

explanation.surface: People quitting a habit take up a fresh line of underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Women's or girls' pants are underwear, in British usage.

clue.text: Put on film about essential sailor's workwear

indicators.note: about says put on plus film go around the other letters, split between them

parts.note: to don clothes is to put them on
ET is the Spielberg film about an extraterrestrial
key means essential or crucial
Jack, as in Jack Tar, is a traditional name for a sailor; the 's is just the possessive

explanation.surface: Someone puts on a film about what a sailor needs for work.
explanation.definitionFit: This heavy hip-length coat with a shoulder patch is traditional British labourers' wear.

clue.text: Prepare ward shortly for 6

definitions.note: 6 refers to the answer at 6 down, a cape or screen

parts.note: to do something such as a meal is to prepare it

indicators.note: shortly says the word for ward is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: a ward is a minor in the care of a guardian

explanation.surface: Instructions to get a hospital ward ready quickly for a patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 is the answer to 6 down, CLOAK.
explanation.definitionFit: A domino is a loose hooded cloak worn with a mask at masquerades.

clue.text: Stocking aid supporting artery to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A support stocking helps an artery to some degree.
explanation.definitionFit: A band worn on the leg holds a stocking up, so it is an aid to it.

clue.text: Cruel base swaggering Three Musketeers' cry?

indicators.note: swaggering suggests strutting about, so the letters of cruel base are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A villain struts about, and the heroes of Dumas cry out against him.
explanation.definitionFit: This mild French oath is what Dumas's Musketeers, being French, might exclaim; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Result of guarantee Republican's conceded

indicators.note: conceded means given up, so the letter for Republican is dropped

parts.note: to ensure something is to guarantee it
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: An election result is guaranteed after the Republican conceded.
explanation.definitionFit: To follow as a consequence is to result, as in chaos will result.

clue.text: Drink demijohn in draught, knocking it all back

indicators.note: knocking back means downing a drink, but here it says the whole assembly is read backwards
in says the half name goes inside the word for a draught

parts.note: a draught is a current of air
demi means half, so this is half of the name john

explanation.surface: Someone downs a whole bottle of wine standing in a chilly breeze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demijohn' looks like a big wine bottle but splits as demi (half) of a name. 'knocking it all back' reverses AJOIR, the result of 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: This Spanish red wine from the region of the same name is a drink.

clue.text: Fold note in suit

indicators.note: in says the note goes inside the word for a suit

parts.note: a suit in law is a case
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A sharp fold appears in the trousers of a suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' suggests clothing, which fits the fold, but it is a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A line pressed or wrinkled into fabric or paper is a fold.

clue.text: One wearing gloves turns over private bank

indicators.note: turns tells us the word for over is turned backwards

parts.note: up can mean over, as in time is up
a GI is a US private soldier
a ship lists or banks when it leans to one side

explanation.surface: A man in gloves flips through a private bank's statement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One wearing gloves' suggests a burglar or surgeon; it is a boxer.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer fights wearing padded gloves, so is one wearing gloves.

clue.text: Frames second sporting trophy

parts.note: the Ashes is the cricket trophy contested by England and Australia

explanation.surface: Someone frames a second sporting trophy for display.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes is the Test cricket series and trophy between England and Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Window sashes are the sliding frames that hold the glass panes.

clue.text: After gym, I got into slight brief nightwear

indicators.note: after means the gym letters come before what follows

parts.note: PE is physical education, the school gym lesson

indicators.note: got into says the letter I is placed inside the shortened word
brief means cut short, so the last letter of the word goes

parts.note: to slight someone is to ignore them

explanation.surface: After a workout, someone squeezes into some slight, skimpy nightwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' cuts IGNORE to IGNOR, and 'got into' puts I inside it to make IGNOIR.
explanation.definitionFit: This loose light dressing gown is a woman's garment worn over a nightdress.
